### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/scenarios`, touching **51** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**38** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 256a4b725116859f891160ad71b21c2e092d1fb0`.

⛔ **16** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 51 pages)`
- **8** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **222** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **159** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **159**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **0** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 256a4b725116859f891160ad71b21c2e092d1fb0` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `31a1b575b82d8d710498d2e4ce2e4862e5efcaca` — the merge of head `584e0ffe3fc18b186cc88bb27c0fa96d3312fc8f` into base `256a4b725116859f891160ad71b21c2e092d1fb0`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 31a1b575b82d8d710498d2e4ce2e4862e5efcaca && git checkout 31a1b575b82d8d710498d2e4ce2e4862e5efcaca
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 256a4b725116859f891160ad71b21c2e092d1fb0 584e0ffe3fc18b186cc88bb27c0fa96d3312fc8f && git checkout -B drift-repro 256a4b725116859f891160ad71b21c2e092d1fb0 && git merge --no-ff 584e0ffe3fc18b186cc88bb27c0fa96d3312fc8f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 256a4b725116859f891160ad71b21c2e092d1fb0
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 256a4b725116859f891160ad71b21c2e092d1fb0` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 · ACCEPT · #30883 · 2026-11-06T15:21Z

Head-sha: `584e0ffe3fc18b186cc88bb27c0fa96d3312fc8f`

- **Shape:** 31 files (+1025/−83). They sit only in the private test package `@objectstack/scenarios` and in `docs/qa/scenarios` (8 cards gain the row-scope tag, plus the README). The card schema gains no key, and no package is published. `Fixes #30883`. `skip-changeset` is right for a private package.
- **Ruling:** item 2 is built as ruled B by the maintainer at 2026-11-06T14:17Z, and the ruling is recorded on #30883. Item 4 follows the revision in 6682060124.
- **Read in the diff:**
  - `observe.ts` rule 4 grades the object's last coded answer to a non-write call as `refused <code>`, and only when the turn sent no write on that object. A read that was retried and succeeded does not count.
  - `gradeOperation(..., { validation })` splits the `write_validation` operation into `agent:refused:<code>-or-withheld` and `platform:refused:<code>` + `platform:no-write`. A probe that was never run fails both platform checks with "not observed", never a pass.
  - `runHalf` sends the probe after the turn as the same persona's key over `tools/call` (`HttpApp.callTool`). A probe that throws is recorded in `res.error`.
- **Gates:** per os-dev-report 6688321669, 53 of 53 derived gates exit 0 after a whole-tree build, and `--ran` shows 0 NOT-MEASURED. The probe was measured live on `examples/app-todo`: create and update answered `VALIDATION_FAILED` with 0 writes, and the valid control was applied. CI on this head: 35 success, 18 skipped, 0 failed. Mergeable: clean.
- **Accepted deviations (not blocking):**
  - The `asksToCorrect` phrase list is broad (`missing`, `required`, `invalid`). An agent that writes nothing and mentions any of those words passes the agent half. The platform half still measures the rule on every run, so this is the ruling's intended leniency.
  - In `orchestrate.ts`, the new `probeValues` sits between `personaOfUser` and its old JSDoc, so `personaOfUser` loses its doc comment. This rides the next touch of the file.
- **Out of scope:** the first run's iterate reply stays an open gap, as the report says.
- `check-governed-merges --pr 30972`: NOT governed, 1108 lines (≤ 3000). Auto-merge lands it on green, and the queue builds it on top of #30938.
